precepts.text: Before the flood our diet was herbs and seeds, and to every beast of the earth God gave every green herb for meat. Even the lions and the tigers and the bears ate herbs and vegetables; nobody ate meat until Genesis 9:3. That is why the animals did not eat each other.
precepts.point: I do set my bow in the cloud: the rainbow was first created here, a token of the covenant that the water shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh. It has nothing to do with LGBT.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
After the flood, “God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth.” Why replenish? Because God killed everybody on the planet. People say God is all love; then they have never read the Bible. He is all love when you obey, but he is also a great and terrible God.

Then: “Every moving thing that liveth shall be meat for you; even as the green herb have I given you all things.” This is the first time meat was introduced into our diet. Genesis 1 shows the diet before: “Behold, I have given you every herb bearing seed, which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree, in the which is the fruit of a tree yielding seed; to you it shall be for meat.” Our diet was herbs and seeds.

And not only ours: “to every beast of the earth, and to every fowl of the air, and to every thing that creepeth upon the earth, wherein there is life, I have given every green herb for meat: and it was so.” Even the lions, the tigers and the bears ate herbs and vegetables. Nobody ate meat until Genesis 9:3. So when someone asks how the animals on the ark did not eat each other, the answer is that their diet was herbs and vegetables. When God introduced meat to us after the flood, the carnivores came with it.

Even then God set a limit: “But flesh with the life thereof, which is the blood thereof, shall ye not eat.” Do not eat anything with blood in it. And he gave a sign: “I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.” The rainbow was first created there, as a promise that the waters would no more become a flood to destroy all flesh, and it has nothing to do with LGBT.

precepts.text: Adam, of whom come we all, and the people also whom thou hast chosen.
precepts.point: God made the world for Israel's sake, and the saints shall take the kingdom.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
People like to say the Israelites stole the Canaanites' land. We stole nothing; the land was ours, and anything a slave owns belongs to his master. Noah gave the prophecy: “Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren.” Then he is more specific: “Blessed be the Lord God of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant.” Israel comes out of Shem, so the Canaanites shall be the servants of Israel. “God shall enlarge Japheth, and he shall dwell in the tents of Shem”. Whose tents would Japheth be living in? Shem's, the Israelites'. Everything belongs to Shem.

At Genesis 9 there were no twelve tribes yet. Israel does not come into being until Jacob's name is changed in Genesis 32, so Noah speaks in terms of Shem, Ham and Japheth. 2 Esdras 6:54 brings it forward to the chosen people: “And after these, Adam also, whom thou madest lord of all thy creatures: of him come we all, and the people also whom thou hast chosen.” Then the part that was wanted, verse 55: “All this have I spoken before thee, O Lord, because thou madest the world for our sakes”. God made the world for our sake.

Psalm 82 was read as going with Esdras and Daniel. “God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.” Verse 6: “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” We are not the Most High, but we are the powers of this earth, the judges of the whole planet. The whole earth belongs to the Israelites.

Verse 5 shows it was always meant to be that way: “They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness: all the foundations of the earth are out of course.” All means everything. If the Israelites are not ruling the planet with God's commandments and laws, everything is out of line, out of the natural way God made it, and there is gross darkness among the people everywhere else. So Canaan being made a servant is part of God's whole plan: the world was made for the chosen, and everything goes back to them.

precepts.text: The kingdom shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High.
precepts.point: God made the world for Israel's sake, and the saints shall take the kingdom.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
After Esdras showed that God made the world for our sakes, Daniel 7:27 gives the next prophecy: “And the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High”. What is under the whole heaven is the planet earth. The earth shall be given to the people of the saints of the Most High.

Psalm 148:14 shows who the saints are: “He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel”. Even means indeed: indeed the children of Israel. The Israelites are the saints. Everything on this planet is going back to the Israelites, including the planet itself.

Daniel goes on: “whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him.” Everybody is going to obey Christ. “Hitherto is the end of the matter”: that is the whole plan of God. “As for me Daniel, my cogitations much troubled me”, meaning his thoughts troubled him, “and my countenance changed in me: but I kept the matter in my heart.”

This is the end of what began with Noah's words over Canaan. Canaan is a servant of servants and Japheth dwells in the tents of Shem, because the dominion under the whole heaven belongs to Shem's chosen seed. From there the class went to Jeremiah 34 to show what it cost Israel when we disobeyed the year of release and would not let our own brethren go free.

precepts.text: One just child is better than a thousand ungodly; replenish the earth with righteous seed.
precepts.point: Noah and his sons were told to replenish the earth after the flood, and the earth is replenished with righteous children; a multitude of ungodly children profits nothing.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
Noah and his sons were told to “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth” after the flood. But the earth is replenished with righteous children. “Desire not a multitude of unprofitable children, neither delight in ungodly sons. Though they multiply, rejoice not in them, except the fear of the Lord be with them.”

A multitude of ungodly children profits nothing: “one that is just is better than a thousand; and better it is to die without children, than to have them that are ungodly.” Replenish the earth with righteous seed.

precepts.text: The wolf dwells with the lamb and a little child leads them; the animals return to their original state when things are set back in order.
precepts.point: The fear and dread of man upon the beasts is not how it was in the beginning, and not how it will remain; the original relationship between man and the animals will be restored.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
After the flood “the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth”. That is not how it was in the beginning, and it is not how it will remain. Isaiah shows the animals returning to their original state when things are set back in order: “The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; and the calf and the young lion and the fatling together; and a little child shall lead them.”

“the lion shall eat straw like the ox”, the sucking child plays on the hole of the asp, and “They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain: for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea.” The original relationship between man and the animals will be restored.

precepts.text: Be not unsatiable in any dainty thing nor too greedy upon meats; excess of meats bringeth sickness.
precepts.point: Fish is meat; all flesh is not the same flesh, but the flesh of beasts, of fishes, and of birds are all flesh. Every creature of God is good for what it was made for, and it is sanctified by the word of God, and the word that sanctifies what may be eaten is the dietary law.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
“Every moving thing that liveth shall be meat for you” is the introduction of man eating meat. The Most High did not give man a new stomach; the body was already made for it and it lay dormant until after the flood.

Having the liberty to eat meat does not mean eating without balance. “My son, prove thy soul in thy life, and see what is evil for it, and give not that unto it. For all things are not profitable for all men, neither hath every soul pleasure in every thing.” “Be not unsatiable in any dainty thing, nor too greedy upon meats: For excess of meats bringeth sickness, and surfeiting will turn into choler. By surfeiting have many perished; but he that taketh heed prolongeth his life.”

precepts.text: The law of the beasts makes a difference between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.
precepts.point: Fish is meat; all flesh is not the same flesh, but the flesh of beasts, of fishes, and of birds are all flesh. Every creature of God is good for what it was made for, and it is sanctified by the word of God, and the word that sanctifies what may be eaten is the dietary law.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
“Every moving thing that liveth shall be meat for you” does not mean you could eat everything. The law of what may be eaten was already understood; Noah had already taken the clean beasts by sevens and the unclean by two. Moses lays out the same thing: “This is the law of the beasts, and of the fowl, and of every living creature that moveth in the waters, and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth: To make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.”

There is a beast that may be eaten and a beast that may not be eaten. The doctrine that says you can pray over anything and eat it is a seducing spirit and a doctrine of devils.

precepts.text: Commanding to abstain from meats is a doctrine of devils; the creature is sanctified by the word of God, which is the dietary law.
precepts.point: Fish is meat; all flesh is not the same flesh, but the flesh of beasts, of fishes, and of birds are all flesh. Every creature of God is good for what it was made for, and it is sanctified by the word of God, and the word that sanctifies what may be eaten is the dietary law.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
Paul warns that “in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils”, among them “commanding to abstain from meats, which God hath created to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth.” Commanding to abstain from meats is a doctrine of devils; the Most High gave meat to man here in Genesis 9:3.

But read the whole thing. “For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving: For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” Every creature of God is good for what it was made for, and it is sanctified by the word of God. The word that sanctifies what may be eaten is the dietary law, the law of the beasts that makes a difference between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not. So the doctrine that says you can pray over anything and eat it is itself the seducing spirit and doctrine of devils.

precepts.text: All flesh is not the same flesh; there is flesh of beasts, of fishes, and of birds, so fish is meat.
precepts.point: Fish is meat; all flesh is not the same flesh, but the flesh of beasts, of fishes, and of birds are all flesh. Every creature of God is good for what it was made for, and it is sanctified by the word of God, and the word that sanctifies what may be eaten is the dietary law.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
Fish is meat. “All flesh is not the same flesh: but there is one kind of flesh of men, another flesh of beasts, another of fishes, and another of birds.” The flesh of beasts, of fishes, and of birds are not the same flesh, but they are all flesh. “God giveth it a body as it hath pleased him, and to every seed his own body.”

So when the Most High says “Every moving thing that liveth shall be meat for you”, fish is included as meat, and it is under the same dietary law that sanctifies what may be eaten.

precepts.text: The word is true from the beginning, and the righteous judgments, the laws, endure for ever.
precepts.point: The law against eating flesh with the blood was given to Adam and is still in place with Noah; the word is true from the beginning.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
“But flesh with the life thereof, which is the blood thereof, shall ye not eat.” This law was given to Adam and is still in place with Noah. “Thy word is true from the beginning: and every one of thy righteous judgments endureth for ever.”

The word is true from the beginning, and the righteous judgments, the laws, endure for ever. The law against eating flesh with the blood did not start with Moses; it was there from the beginning and it endures.

precepts.text: Adam was given the breath of life, the commandments, and a commandment to love the way of the Most High; the peoples after him despised the commandments.
precepts.point: The law against eating flesh with the blood was given to Adam and is still in place with Noah; the word is true from the beginning.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
Ezra goes back to the beginning: the Most High “spakest at the beginning, when thou didst plant the earth, and that thyself alone, and commandedst the people”. He gave “a body unto Adam without soul” and “didst breathe into him the breath of life”; that breath of life is the commandments. “And unto him thou gavest commandment to love thy way: which he transgressed”.

So Adam had commandments, and the law against eating flesh with the blood was among what was given to him. From Adam “came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number. And every people walked after their own will, and did wonderful things before thee, and despised thy commandments.” The peoples after Adam despised the commandments, but the commandments were there, and they are still in place with Noah. The word is true from the beginning.

precepts.text: The coats of skins were the first sacrifice; the beast stood in place of Adam and Eve.
precepts.point: That is the scapegoat: it takes the wrongdoings, mistakes, and faults of others and places them on the animal. That is why Cain and Abel were bringing offerings, because they knew of the sacrifice from Genesis 3.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
“at the hand of every beast will I require it”: the Most High requiring blood at the hand of every beast is animal sacrifice, still in place with Noah, passed down generation to generation. It begins in Genesis 3. “Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them.” Those coats of skins were the first sacrifice.

The judgment for sin has always been death. When Eve sinned and caused Adam to sin, either they had to die, or something had to stand in their place. The beast whose skin clothed them stood in for Adam and Eve; the blood of the animal stood in for them.

precepts.text: Cain and Abel brought offerings, proving the sacrifice was known and passed down.
precepts.point: That is the scapegoat: it takes the wrongdoings, mistakes, and faults of others and places them on the animal. That is why Cain and Abel were bringing offerings, because they knew of the sacrifice from Genesis 3.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
“Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord. And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering: But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect.”

Cain and Abel were bringing offerings because they knew of the sacrifice from Genesis 3, when the beast stood in place of Adam and Eve. That proves the sacrifice was known and passed down generation to generation, and it is still in place when the Most High tells Noah he will require blood at the hand of every beast.

precepts.text: The scapegoat is presented alive to make an atonement, standing in for the faults of others.
precepts.point: That is the scapegoat: it takes the wrongdoings, mistakes, and faults of others and places them on the animal. That is why Cain and Abel were bringing offerings, because they knew of the sacrifice from Genesis 3.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
The blood required at the hand of every beast is the animal standing in for man. That is the scapegoat. “Aaron shall cast lots upon the two goats; one lot for the Lord, and the other lot for the scapegoat.” The goat on which the Lord’s lot fell is offered “for a sin offering”, and the scapegoat “shall be presented alive before the Lord, to make an atonement with him, and to let him go for a scapegoat into the wilderness.”

The scapegoat takes the wrongdoings, mistakes, and faults of others and places them on the animal. That is what the coats of skins were for Adam and Eve, and what Cain and Abel knew when they brought their offerings: the judgment for sin has always been death, and the animal stands in the sinner’s place.

precepts.text: Christ came not to destroy the law or the prophets; not one jot or one tittle shall pass from the law.
precepts.point: The laws were never done away with; Christ came not to destroy the law but to fulfil, and not one jot or tittle passes from the law.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
“Whoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed”: life for life. This law is given to Noah, way before Moses, so it cannot be dismissed as the law of Moses.

The laws were never done away with. Christ says “Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil. For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.” Not one jot or tittle passes from the law, and that includes the law of life for life given here.

precepts.text: Look upon the rainbow and praise Him that made it; the hands of the Most High bended it.
precepts.point: The world has taken that same bow, the token of the covenant, and turned it into the symbol of sodomy. The spiritual eyes will see what that means: the great city is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
The bow in the cloud, the rainbow, is the token of the covenant between the Most High and the earth. “Look upon the rainbow, and praise him that made it; very beautiful it is in the brightness thereof. It compasseth the heaven about with a glorious circle, and the hands of the most High have bended it.”

His hands bended it. When you see the bow you are to praise Him that made it, and remember the covenant it stands for.

precepts.text: The great city is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt; the place that flies the bow as a symbol of sodomy identifies itself.
precepts.point: The world has taken that same bow, the token of the covenant, and turned it into the symbol of sodomy. The spiritual eyes will see what that means: the great city is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
The world has taken that same bow, the token of the covenant the Most High set in the cloud, and turned it into the symbol of sodomy. The spiritual eyes will see what that means. Revelation speaks of “the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.”

The great city is spiritually called Sodom. The place that flies the bow as a symbol of sodomy identifies itself.

precepts.text: The Lord is longsuffering, not willing that any should perish; but the day of the Lord will come, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat.
precepts.point: The waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh. The next time the destruction is not water but fire, when the day of the Lord comes and the elements melt with fervent heat.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
“the waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh.” That promise stands, but it does not mean there is no more destruction. The next time it is not water but fire.

“The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.” The same longsuffering that waited in the days of Noah waits now. “But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night; in the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat, the earth also and the works that are therein shall be burned up.” When the day of the Lord comes, the elements melt with fervent heat.

precepts.text: Noah was the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness.
precepts.point: Ham saw the nakedness of his father and did not cover him; Shem and Japheth went backward and covered their father without looking. The commandments concerning nakedness were being applied; Leviticus 18 opens those laws.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
Noah drank of the wine and was drunken, but understand Noah’s heart. He was “a preacher of righteousness”, the eighth person saved when the Most High “spared not the old world” and brought “in the flood upon the world of the ungodly”.

He preached repentance for around a hundred years, and everyone he knew outside his house drowned. That is the heavy heart behind the wine. Noah drank too much, but he remained righteous in the eyes of the Most High.

precepts.text: Noah was found perfect and righteous and was left as a remnant unto the earth.
precepts.point: Ham saw the nakedness of his father and did not cover him; Shem and Japheth went backward and covered their father without looking. The commandments concerning nakedness were being applied; Leviticus 18 opens those laws.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
Noah was still perfect and righteous after this. “Noah was found perfect and righteous; in the time of wrath he was taken in exchange for the world; therefore was he left as a remnant unto the earth, when the flood came. An everlasting covenant was made with him, that all flesh should perish no more by the flood.”

He drank too much and was uncovered within his tent, but one fall does not undo righteousness. He remained righteous in the eyes of the Most High.

precepts.text: A just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again.
precepts.point: Ham saw the nakedness of his father and did not cover him; Shem and Japheth went backward and covered their father without looking. The commandments concerning nakedness were being applied; Leviticus 18 opens those laws.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why: “For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.” Noah was a just man. He fell here, drinking of the wine until he was drunken, but a just man rises up again. One fall does not undo righteousness; Noah was still perfect and righteous in the eyes of the Most High.

precepts.text: Wine is for those of heavy hearts, to remember misery no more; that was Noah after the flood.
precepts.point: Ham saw the nakedness of his father and did not cover him; Shem and Japheth went backward and covered their father without looking. The commandments concerning nakedness were being applied; Leviticus 18 opens those laws.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
“Give strong drink unto him that is ready to perish, and wine unto those that be of heavy hearts. Let him drink, and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.” Wine is for those of heavy hearts, and that was Noah after the flood.

He preached repentance for around a hundred years, and everyone he knew outside his house drowned. He drank too much, but he remained righteous in the eyes of the Most High.

precepts.text: God speaks in a dream, in a vision of the night, and seals the instruction of men.
precepts.point: Blessed be the Lord God of Shem: it was revealed that the Messiah and the righteous seed would come through Shem.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
Noah was asleep, so how did he know what his younger son had done unto him? “For God speaketh once, yea twice, yet man perceiveth it not. In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falleth upon men, in slumberings upon the bed; Then he openeth the ears of men, and sealeth their instruction”.

The Most High speaks to man in a dream, in a vision of the night. Noah awoke from his wine and knew, because the Lord told him while deep sleep was upon him.

precepts.text: The Lord God reveals His secret unto His servants the prophets.
precepts.point: Blessed be the Lord God of Shem: it was revealed that the Messiah and the righteous seed would come through Shem.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
“Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.” Noah was a preacher of righteousness, a servant of the Most High, and the Lord revealed to him what his younger son had done while he slept.

Out of that revelation came the words: “Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren”, and “Blessed be the Lord God of Shem”. It was revealed that the Messiah and the righteous seed would come through Shem.

precepts.text: Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed; the only cleansing of the land is the blood of the shedder.
precepts.point: That judgment was instituted back in the days of Noah, and Moses carried it forward in the statutes given to Israel, for the Lord himself dwells among the children of Israel.

note.label: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
“So ye shall not pollute the land wherein ye are: for blood it defileth the land: and the land cannot be cleansed of the blood that is shed therein, but by the blood of him that shed it.” The murderer who escapes his judgment leaves the land polluted.

That judgment was instituted back in the days of Noah: “Whoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of God made he man.” The only cleansing of the land is the blood of the shedder.

Moses carried it forward in the statutes given to Israel, and the reason is given: “Defile not therefore the land which ye shall inhabit, wherein I dwell: for I the Lord dwell among the children of Israel.”

precepts.text: The Most High requires the blood of a man's life at the hand of every man's brother.
precepts.point: Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, because David had killed the man. The true baptism is not the dipping in water but the answer of a good conscience toward the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God”: David says this because he had killed the man. The Most High told Noah, “surely your blood of your lives will I require; at the hand of every beast will I require it, and at the hand of man; at the hand of every man’s brother will I require the life of man.” The Most High requires the blood of a man's life at the hand of every man's brother, so David stood guilty of blood.

The true baptism is not the dipping in water but the answer of a good conscience toward the Most High. That is what David is asking for: to be delivered from that guilt so his tongue can sing aloud of the Most High's righteousness.

precepts.text: Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed, for in the image of God made he man; David was guilty for shedding this man's blood.
precepts.point: Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, because David had killed the man. The true baptism is not the dipping in water but the answer of a good conscience toward the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“Whoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of God made he man.” David was guilty for shedding this man's blood, and by this word his own blood was owed. That is the bloodguiltiness he asks the God of his salvation to deliver him from.

Man is made in the image of God, so shedding his blood is required at the hand of every man's brother. David could not wash that away in water; the true baptism is the answer of a good conscience toward the Most High, and only the Most High could deliver him.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 4 Kingdom Vision

precepts.why:
God sets his bow in the cloud as the token of a covenant between himself and the earth. When clouds gather, the bow appears and he remembers his covenant with every living creature: the waters will not again become a flood destroying all flesh.

The rainbow already existed around the heavenly throne. God established that heavenly thing upon the earth as an everlasting covenant. The same pattern will appear with other things John sees: what God set before him in heaven was also shown and established below.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: “Neither shall there any more be a flood to destroy the earth.” “I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth”: that is the rainbow. This is what our sons and daughters must learn.

points: And I will establish my covenant with you; neither shall all flesh be cut off any more by the waters of a flood; neither shall there any more be a flood to destroy the earth.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: And God said, This is the token of the covenant which I make between me and you and every living creature that is with you, for perpetual generations: I do set my bow in the cloud. The bow is the rainbow.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: And it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth. And it shall come to pass, when I bring a cloud over the earth, that the bow shall be seen in the cloud. The rainbow shall be seen in the cloud.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: And I will remember my covenant, which is between me and you and every living creature of all flesh; and the waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: And the bow shall be in the cloud; and I will look upon it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is upon the earth. And God said unto Noah, This is the token of the covenant, which I have established between me and all flesh that is upon the earth.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth. Why replenish the earth? Because God killed everybody on the planet. You have to imagine that. People say God is all love; then you have never read the Bible. He is all love when you obey, but the scripture also says he is a great and terrible God.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

points: Every moving thing that liveth shall be meat for you: this is the first time meat was introduced into our diet. In Genesis 1 the diet was herbs and vegetables; after the flood he introduces meat. But flesh with the life thereof, which is the blood thereof, shall ye not eat: do not eat anything with blood in it.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

points: I do set my bow in the cloud: the rainbow was first created here, a token of the covenant that the water shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh. It has nothing to do with LGBT.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

points: Cursed be Canaan, a servant of servants unto his brethren.
God made the world for Israel's sake, and the saints shall take the kingdom.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

points: Noah and his sons were told to replenish the earth after the flood, and the earth is replenished with righteous children; a multitude of ungodly children profits nothing.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

points: The fear and dread of man upon the beasts is not how it was in the beginning, and not how it will remain; the original relationship between man and the animals will be restored.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

points: This is the introduction of man eating meat. The Most High did not give man a new stomach; the body was already made for it and it lay dormant until after the flood.
Having the liberty to eat meat does not mean eating without balance; be not too greedy upon meats, for excess of meats brings sickness.
The law of what may be eaten was already understood; you could not eat everything. The doctrine that says you can pray over anything and eat it is a seducing spirit and a doctrine of devils.

Fish is meat; all flesh is not the same flesh, but the flesh of beasts, of fishes, and of birds are all flesh. Every creature of God is good for what it was made for, and it is sanctified by the word of God, and the word that sanctifies what may be eaten is the dietary law.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

points: The law against eating flesh with the blood was given to Adam and is still in place with Noah; the word is true from the beginning.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

points: The Most High requiring blood at the hand of every beast is animal sacrifice, still in place with Noah, passed down generation to generation.
The judgment for sin has always been death. When Eve sinned and caused Adam to sin, either they had to die, or something had to stand in their place; the blood of the animal stood in for them.

That is the scapegoat: it takes the wrongdoings, mistakes, and faults of others and places them on the animal. That is why Cain and Abel were bringing offerings, because they knew of the sacrifice from Genesis 3.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

points: Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed: life for life. This law is way before Moses, so it cannot be dismissed as the law of Moses.
The laws were never done away with; Christ came not to destroy the law but to fulfil, and not one jot or tittle passes from the law.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

points: The covenant established here is with Noah, his seed, and every living creature: all flesh shall never again be cut off by the waters of a flood.
This is a general covenant with all flesh. The covenant with Israel is found in Jeremiah 31.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

points: The bow in the cloud, the rainbow, is the token of the covenant between the Most High and the earth; it compasses the heaven about with a glorious circle, and His hands bended it.

The world has taken that same bow, the token of the covenant, and turned it into the symbol of sodomy. The spiritual eyes will see what that means: the great city is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

points: The waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh. The next time the destruction is not water but fire, when the day of the Lord comes and the elements melt with fervent heat.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

points: Shem, Ham, and Japheth went forth out of the ark and the whole earth was overspread from them. Ham dwelt in what is called Africa; Shem in the land mass toward Arabia; Japheth went into Europe.

Ham is the father of Canaan, and Canaan dwelt in the land later called the land of Israel. That is how you know the land of Israel is a part of Africa; the maps separate Israel from Africa so that the connection is not made.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

points: Understand Noah's heart: he preached repentance for around a hundred years, and everyone he knew outside his house drowned. Strong drink is for him that is ready to perish and wine for those of heavy hearts; Noah drank too much, but he remained righteous in the eyes of the Most High.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

points: Ham saw the nakedness of his father and did not cover him; Shem and Japheth went backward and covered their father without looking. The commandments concerning nakedness were being applied; Leviticus 18 opens those laws.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

points: Noah was asleep, so how did he know what his younger son had done? The Most High speaks to man in a dream, in a vision of the night, and reveals His secret unto His servants the prophets; Noah was a preacher of righteousness, and the Lord told him.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

points: Cursed be Canaan: a servant of servants unto his brethren.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

points: Blessed be the Lord God of Shem: it was revealed that the Messiah and the righteous seed would come through Shem.
